newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - bracing for lots of supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - bracing for lots of supply.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices in late afternoon trade on Monday fell from one-eighth to one-quarter of a point as traders fretted about an unusually large amount of new issues scheduled for sale this week.
As much as $4.8 billion of new offerings are expected to be sold this week, with nearly half of this sum set for Tuesday, when almost $2.2 million of new debt will come to market.
This week's negotiated calender includes $459 million of New York City Transit Authority revenue bonds, $211 million of Chicago O'Hare Airport bonds, and $175 million of Texas Housing revenue issues.

Some of the big deals on the competitive calender are $500 million of California general obligation bonds, which are scheduled for Tuesday, along with $170 million of Minnesota general obligations, and $150 million of Massachusetts Water Resource Authority revenue bonds.
"We have a pretty large new issue calender. The feeling is you may see some selling to make room," a trader said.
But the trader added that potential buyers appeared to be holding off until they saw whether the new debt was attractively priced.

While around 18 or so bid-wanted lists were being circulated, this was viewed as only moderate selling pressure, traders said. They explained about 30 of such lists, which advertize what bonds institutions wish to sell, would represent heavy selling interest.
The Standard & Poor's Blue List, a gauge of secondary market activity, stood at about $1.3 billion, a level that is considered medium.
"Nothing went on today. I'd classify it as a slow Monday, with a bias to the bid side," a trader said.

Market experts divided over precisely how much prices were marked down, with one saying prices fell from one-quarter to as much as three-eighths of one point, while another said dollar bonds were from unchanged to slightly softer.

Actively traded issues included Dade County Florida Water and Sewer Sytems Revenues of October 2025, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon. They were bid at 5.76 percent, NET, up two basis points from levels seen on Friday.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority of March 2020, which carry a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.73 percent, NET, against the 5.72 percent level seen on Friday.
The December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade continued to lose ground to the U.S. Treasury bond futures, with the MOB spread easing to 100 ticks.
This marks a fairly sharp drop from mid-summer, when the municipal bond contracts enjoyed around a 170-tick premium to Treasuries.
The December municipal bond futures fell 19 ticks to 114-6/32, while the benchmark Treasury December bond futures fell seven ticks to 111-2/32.
